declared.title: Can There Ever Be Too Many Options? A Meta-Analytic Review of Choice Overload
declared.foundIn: nommée dans la consigne de la session ; titre relevé sur la recherche Crossref « can there ever be too many options meta-analytic review choice overload » du 2026-11-22 : contrôle d'identité plus faible

population: 50 published and unpublished experiments on the number of options (63 conditions); countries not given in the abstract

findings.text: Across 50 experiments, the mean effect of a larger set on choice overload (lower satisfaction or motivation to choose, pooled) was virtually zero, with large differences between studies

support.sentence: In a meta-analysis of 63 conditions from 50 published and unpublished experiments (N = 5,036), we found a mean effect size of virtually zero but considerable variance between studies.

findings.text: Some conditions seemed necessary for too many options to hurt, but none was found that reliably produces the effect

support.sentence: While further analyses indicated several potentially important preconditions for choice overload, no sufficient conditions could be identified.

limits: mostly consumer choices in the lab and the field, not life choices
the mean effect is said in words (« virtually zero »), no number in the abstract; outcomes pooled
its first author led failed tests of the effect (scheibehenne-2009-moderators): not independent of that line
a later meta-analysis that codes moderators finds an effect under conditions (chernev-2015-overload)
